prompt:
Scene:
A square overhead-angled view of the crossing of a gothic cathedral, where nave, transepts and choir meet under a central square of rib-vaulting. Deep indigo stone floor inlaid with pale stone bands.

Subject:
A large volumetric holographic cross stands vertically in the crossing, suspended just above the floor, its beams made of layered cyan light sheets with a warm amber core. Where the cross meets the stone, a circular pool of refracted light spreads outward in fine concentric rings on the floor inlay. Four narrow AR ribbons descend from the four rib-vault corners, each touching one arm of the cross.

Important details:
Stone floor inlay must be physically correct: pale stone bands form a cross pattern matching the crossing, with age wear, grout lines, and tiny chips. The volumetric cross must have clear layered depth — multiple parallel light sheets, not one flat shape. Light scatter onto floor must follow real refraction physics: concentric soft rings, not hard circles. Color palette: cyan sheets, amber core, indigo stone, pale floor bands.

Use case:
Hologram Cathedral Nave single study 5/5, focusing on a volumetric cross at the crossing.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no crucifix corpus, no realistic Christ figure, no brand engravings on the floor, no human silhouettes, no candles in frame.
